# Yunhao Luo — Personal Website

> The personal site of Yunhao Luo, an AI researcher focused on the agentic web — web agents, website generation, and emerging standards for making the web agent-friendly — with a foundation in character animation, physics-based simulation, and real-time rendering. The site is shaped like a game: an HD-2D, Souls-inspired hub world ("Crepusculum Dream") where each landmark leads to an area of content.

Yunhao Luo is an AI researcher at Huawei Canada's Web Technology Lab. He previously researched real-time GPU fluid simulation at Ubisoft La Forge and holds an M.Sc. in Computer Science from McGill University; his thesis work received the Best Presentation Award at MIG '21.

For AI agents: this site registers WebMCP tools on `document.modelContext`. Four global tools stay available everywhere: `list-site-pages`, `get-about-me`, `goto-site-page`, and `set-language`. The remaining tools follow the active page and are removed when the visitor leaves it. On every content page, `get-page-overview` and `focus-page-section` are re-registered with that page's own description, section enum, returned data, and visible effect.

Page tools: Home provides `walk-hero-to-landmark` and `get-hero-status`; Projects provides `get-fluid-simulation`; Research provides the read-only `get-publications` and `get-citation` plus the separate `copy-citation` action; Mods provides `get-mod-details` and `goto_workshop_page`; The Zine provides `read-zine-piece`; About provides `get-photography-captions`.

## Areas

- [Home](/#/): the explorable HD-2D hub world; every landmark below lives here
- [Projects](/#/projects): write-up and captured demos of the real-time GPU liquid simulator built at Ubisoft Montreal (position-based fluids on compute shaders, now part of the Anvil engine)
- [Research](/#/research): first-author publication — Catching and Throwing Control of a Physically Simulated Hand (MIG '21, Best Presentation Award), with abstract, BibTeX, and links
- [Mods](/#/mods): Mizuki Mod — a complete custom Slay the Spire character (78 cards, custom mechanics, Spine-animated sprite)
- [Zine](/#/zine): a modern-poetry zine, presented as readable pages
- [About](/#/about): bio, interests, photography, and the site's WebMCP tool documentation
